Best Kodi Addons in May 2026

By Marcus Eriksson - April 9, 2026

Disclosure: Some links on this page are affiliate links. We may earn a commission if you make a purchase through them, at no additional cost to you.

In this article, we review some of the best Kodi addons for May 2026 on Krypton 17.6. For each addon, you’ll get a short “what it does” summary plus step-by-step install instructions.

NOTE: Kodi is just a media player — what you stream depends on the addon and sources you use. If you want privacy on public Wi-Fi, to reduce ISP throttling, or to access geo-restricted services legally, a VPN can help. See our list of recommended VPN providers for Kodi.

Quick reality check (important): Kodi addon availability changes constantly (repos go offline, forks appear, names get reused). If an install path fails, it’s usually the repository — not your Kodi setup.

1. Overall Best Kodi Addons May 2026

1.1 Neptune Rising Addon

What it’s for: movie + TV browsing with a familiar layout and lots of categories.

Why people use it: simple navigation, broad catalog, and multiple sorting options (genre, language, country).

What to expect: repos and forks have changed over time, so sub-categories and reliability can vary depending on the build you install.

How to install the Neptune Rising addon:

  1. Add the Blamo repository (we described how to do this in the previous article about Kodi).
  2. Open Add-ons — Add-on browser — Install from the repository — Blamo Repo — Video add-ons — Neptune Rising — click Install.

1.2 Placenta Addon

What it’s for: movies + TV with extra sections like Kids, Music, and Fitness.

Why people use it: frequent updates (when the repo is maintained) and a “scraper-style” approach that can surface multiple links for the same title.

What to expect: quality depends on the sources a given version pulls from, and repo stability is the #1 failure point.

How to install the Placenta addon:

  1. Add the Blamo repository (we described how to do this in the previous article about Kodi).
  2. Open Add-ons — Add-on browser — Install from the repository — Blamo Repo — Video add-ons — Placenta — click Install.

1.3 Genesis Reborn Addon

What it’s for: TV shows, series, and movies with richer discovery tools.

Why people use it: extra metadata (like IMDb ratings) plus “trending/top-rated” style lists, and multiple links per title.

What to expect: “reborn” addons often change hands; if links break, it’s usually the repo or scrapers.

How to install the Genesis Reborn addon:

  1. Open Settings — File manager — Add source — type or paste https://jesusboxrepo.xyz/repo — name the repository Jesus Box Repo.
  2. After that, go to Add-ons — Enter add-on browser — Install from zip file — Jesus Box Repo — repository.jesusboxtv-1.0.3.zip.
  3. Open Install from the repository — Jesus Box Repo — Video add-ons — Genesis Reborn — click Install.

1.4 Covenant Addon

What it’s for: a long-running “movies + TV” style addon with straightforward menus.

Why people use it: easy navigation, lots of filters (genre, language, country), and Trakt.tv integration for watchlists.

What to expect: like many classic Kodi names, current functionality depends on the repo/fork you install.

How to install the Covenant addon:

  1. Open Settings — File manager — Add source — type or paste https://aeom.cf/repo/ — name the repository All Eyes on Me.
  2. After that, go to Add-ons — Enter add-on browser — Install from zip file — All Eyes on Me — repository.alleyezonme.zip.
  3. Open Install from the repository — All Eyes on Me — Video add-ons — Covenant — click Install.

1.5 Incursion Addon

What it’s for: an “Exodus-like” browsing experience for movies and series.

Why people use it: many filters (region/language/genre/providers) and lots of alternate links per title.

What to expect: reliability depends on the source ecosystem and whether the repo is actively maintained.

How to install the Incursion addon:

  1. Open Settings — File manager — Add source — type or paste https://fusion.tvaddons.co — name the repository Fusion.
  2. After that, go to Add-ons — Enter add-on browser — Install from zip file — Fusion — repository.xbmchub.zip.
  3. Open Install from the repository — Fusion — Video add-ons — Incursion — click Install.

2. Best Movies and Shows Kodi Addons

2.1 Exodus

What it’s for: a classic “movies + TV” addon layout with categories, sorting, and favorites.

Why people use it: familiar menus, large libraries (depending on sources), and discovery filters (genre, year, ranking, country).

What to expect: “Exodus” is a heavily forked name — working status depends on the specific repo build.

How to install the Exodus addon:

  1. Open Settings — File manager — Add source — type or paste https://archive.org/download/repository.xvbmc — name the repository Repository.XvBMC.
  2. After that, go to Add-ons — Enter add-on browser — Install from zip file — Repository.XvBMC — repository.xvbmc-4.2.0.zip.
  3. Open Install from the repository — Repository.XvBMC — Video add-ons — Incursion — click Install.

2.2 FilmON Simple

What it’s for: curated educational content plus a range of streams.

Why people use it: simple interface and lots of categories (40+), making it easier to browse by topic.

How to install the FilmON Simple addon:

  1. Open Settings — File manager — Add source — type or paste https://fusion.tvaddons.co/ — name the repository TV Add-ons.
  2. After that, go to Add-ons — Enter add-on browser — Install from zip file — TV Add-ons — repository.xbmchub-3.0.0.zip.
  3. Open Install from the repository — TV Add-ons — Video add-ons — FilmON Simple — click Install.

2.3 Gaia

What it’s for: a premium-leaning addon that can integrate with paid sources (and may support Usenet/torrent indexers depending on configuration).

Why people use it: more control, more integrations, and better results when paired with legitimate paid services.

What to expect: you can run it “free,” but it’s typically strongest when configured with paid providers.

How to install the Gaia addon:

  1. Open Settings — File manager — Add source — type or paste https://repo.gaiakodi.com/ — name the repository Gaia.
  2. After that, go to Add-ons — Enter add-on browser — Install from zip file — Gaia — repository.gaia.zip.
  3. Open Install from the repository — Gaia — Video add-ons — Gaia — click Install.

3. Best Live TV Kodi Addons

3.1 BBC iPlayer

What it’s for: BBC iPlayer on Kodi — live channels and on-demand content (typically last 30 days).

Key limitation: it generally requires a UK IP address. One way people handle this is to install a VPN service and connect to the UK.

How to install the iPlayer WWW addon:

  1. Open Add-ons — Download Video add-ons — iPlayer WWW — click Install.
  2. Alternative option: click on Search icon — Search Add-ons — enter BBC iPlayer — iPlayer WWW — click Install button.

3.2 cCloud TV

What it’s for: a broad directory of live TV channels across categories.

Why people use it: global channel variety, category browsing, and “most popular” lists for quick picks.

How to install the cCloud TV addon:

  1. Open Settings — File manager — Add source — type or paste https://kdil.co/repo/ — name the repository Kodi Israel.
  2. After that, go to Add-ons — Enter add-on browser — Install from zip file — Kodi Israel — Kodil.zip.
  3. Open Install from the repository — Kodil Repository — Video add-ons — cCloud TV — click Install.

3.3 Channel PEAR

What it’s for: watching TV channels via the Channel PEAR service.

What to expect: many channels require a paid subscription, but some are available for free. HD streams are common, and setup is fast once your account is linked.

How to install the Channel PEAR addon:

  1. Download the zip archive and save it to your device.
  2. Go to Add-ons — Open from zip file — choose the file you previously downloaded — click Install button.
  3. Enter your login and password to benefit all the service features.

4. Best General Video Kodi Addons

4.1 YouTube

What it’s for: YouTube inside Kodi, with subscriptions, history, favorites, and playlists.

Tip: connect your YouTube/Google account after install to unlock the full experience.

How to install the YouTube addon:

  1. As the add-on is available in the official Kodi repository, in the main menu open Add-ons — Download Video add-ons — YouTube — click Install.
  2. Alternative option: click on Search icon — Search Add-ons — enter YouTube — Media sources – YouTube — click Install button.

4.2 TED Talks

What it’s for: TED Talks browsing and playback inside Kodi.

Why people use it: easy access to the full archive, favorites, and popular talks by topic.

How to install the TED Talks addon:

  1. As the add-on is available in the official Kodi repository, in the main menu open Add-ons — Download Video add-ons — TED Talks — click Install.
  2. Alternative option: click on Search icon — Search Add-ons — enter TED Talks — Media sources – TED Talks — click Install button.

4.3 Uranus

What it’s for: general movies + shows with category browsing and Trakt.tv support.

Why people use it: lots of filters (country/language/year/popularity) and familiar navigation.

How to install the Uranus addon:

  1. Add the Blamo repository (we described how to do this in the previous article about Kodi).
  2. After that, go to Add-ons — Enter add-on browser — Install from zip file — Blamo — repository.griffin-0.0.6.zip.
  3. Open Install from the repository — Griffin Repository — Video add-ons — Uranus — click Install.

10. Best Weather Kodi Addons

10.1 Met Office

What it’s for: a clean 5-day forecast with auto-detect and fast load times.

Limitation: this version notes you can select only one location.

How to install the Met Office addon:

10.2 OpenWeatherMap Extended

What it’s for: a more detailed forecast with longer ranges (36 hours up to 2 weeks).

11. Best Maintenance Kodi Addons

This category is about keeping Kodi running smoothly: backups, restores, cache cleanup, and addon management.

11.1 Indigo

What it’s for: maintenance and recovery: clear cache, reset settings, create backups, and restore them.

Why people use it: it bundles common “fix Kodi” tools in one place, which is useful when builds or addons cause instability.

How to install the Indigo addon:

  1. Add the Fusion repository (see Incursion add-on mentioned above).
  2. After that, go to Add-ons — Enter add-on browser — Install from zip file — Fusion — begin-here — program.indigo-.3.0.2.zip.

11.2 Git Browser

What it’s for: installing Kodi addons hosted on GitHub without manually moving files around.

Why people use it: it reduces friction when experimenting with third-party projects and supports most devices that run Kodi.

How to install the Git Browser addon:

  1. Add the Fusion repository (see Incursion add-on mentioned above).
  2. After that, go to Add-ons — Enter add-on browser — Install from zip file — Fusion — Kodi-Repos — English — repository.xbmchub.zip.
  3. Open Install from the repository — Fusion — Services — Git Browser — click Install.

12. Conclusion

Kodi becomes far more useful once you add the right addons for your use case: on-demand video, live TV, sports, fitness, weather, and maintenance tools. If an addon fails to install, check the repository status first — that’s the most common break point.
